answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with one global, single-file admission queue: every new identity must wait its turn for a fixed-rate verification slot, claimed only by doing useful work checked before the next identity is served. A yarrow of fake accounts gains nothing by multiplying, because the queue serves one identity at a time and cannot be bought out; a prism of parallel submissions still funnels into the same narrow gate, and each juniper newcomer joins at the back, so an attacker's tenth identity waits ten times as long as the first.
